original_value: Deep learning based methods have achieved remarkable progress in action recognition. Existing works mainly focus on designing novel deep architectures to achieve video representations learning for action recognition. Most methods treat sampled frames equally and average all the frame-level predictions at the testing stage. However, within a video, discriminative actions may occur sparsely in a few frames and most other frames are irrelevant to the ground truth and may even lead to a wrong prediction. As a result, we think that the strategy of selecting relevant frames would be a further important key to enhance the existing deep learning based action recognition. In this paper, we propose an attentionaware sampling method for action recognition, which aims to discard the irrelevant and misleading frames and preserve the most discriminative frames. We formulate the process of mining key frames from videos as a Markov decision process and train the attention agent through deep reinforcement learning without extra labels. The agent takes features and predictions from the baseline model as input and generates importance scores for all frames. Moreover, our approach is extensible, which can be applied to different existing deep learning based action recognition models. We achieve very competitive action recognition performance on two widely used action recognition datasets.

result.paraphrase: Deep learning methods have made remarkable advances in action recognition. Prior work has largely centered on creating new deep architectures for learning video representations for action recognition. Most approaches treat sampled frames equally and average all frame-level predictions at test time. But in a video, discriminative actions may appear only sparsely in a few frames, while most other frames are irrelevant to the ground truth and can even cause incorrect predictions. Therefore, selecting relevant frames should be an important further step for improving existing deep learning based action recognition. In this paper, we present an attention-aware sampling method for action recognition that discards irrelevant and misleading frames while retaining the most discriminative ones. We cast the task of mining key frames from videos as a Markov decision process and train the attention agent with deep reinforcement learning without extra labels. The agent uses features and predictions from the baseline model as input and outputs importance scores for all frames. In addition, our method is extensible and can be applied to different existing deep learning based action recognition models. We obtain very competitive action recognition performance on two widely used action recognition datasets.
